item.title: 'Global South must shape, not just follow, rules': PM Modi at Brics Summit
item.description: Prime Minister Modi opened the Brics summit, demanding urgent United Nations Security Council reforms. He stressed transforming global governance from privilege to partnership for developing nations. Modi proposed Brics draft ten proposals for inclusive global governance and multilateralism. He also called for a Seafarers Emergency Support Network for maritime workers. The summit aims to empower the Global South as rule-shapers, not rule-takers.

item.title: Brics opposes unilateral trade steps like EU carbon border tax
item.description: In a united front, BRICS countries protested against the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism, deeming it unfair. They underscored the importance of energy security alongside a pragmatic approach toward climate goals, making it clear that fossil fuels remain integral to the energy mix. The alliance urged for actions driven by equity and collective responsibilities, indicating their trust in multilateral efforts to confront global climate challenges.
item.dc:creator: VISHWA MOHAN

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg on how engineers made him return to Musk's X after 3 years in 2026
item.description: In 2026, Mark Zuckerberg made a surprising return to Elon Musk's social network X, seizing the opportunity to unveil Meta's latest AI innovation, Muse. By engaging with specific engineering talent and researchers on X, Zuckerberg aims to leverage diverse online communities for fostering discussions, effectively amplifying Meta's AI initiatives in front of potential developers.

item.title: India to get another major DRDO missile testing range in Bengal
item.description: India is embarking on a pivotal project with the establishment of a new weapon and missile testing range in Junput, West Bengal. This state-of-the-art facility will complement the existing range in Chandipur, Odisha, marking the DRDO's third significant site. The initiative promises to not only bolster national defense capabilities but also promote substantial growth in West Bengal's infrastructure and economy.

item.title: Harvard University has a 'September message' for all international students
item.description: Harvard University has alerted international students about significant F-1 and J-1 visa rule changes. New Department of Homeland Security rules replace the duration of status system with fixed visa end dates. Students re-entering the US after September 15 will face stricter limits and new visa frameworks. Those already in the US before this date will generally retain current protections and benefits.

item.title: Sebi for changes to CAS timing, derivatives settlement prices
item.description: Sebi has put forth new proposals aimed at modifying the Closing Auction Session timings and derivatives pricing. Following the recent launch of the session, traders have noted an uptick in market volatility. The regulator is evaluating two potential options for determining derivative settlement prices, suggesting a shift in market timings to include a transition break and longer trading intervals. Feedback on these proposals is requested by October 3.

item.title: 100 years later, Iowa book that made Ruth Suckow famous is being revived
item.description: Ruth Suckow's remarkable collection 'Iowa Interiors' returns in a special centennial edition, featuring captivating new illustrations by talented artist Claudia McGehee. To complement the reissue, the Hearst Center hosts an exhibition spotlighting McGehee's original artworks. This initiative not only revitalizes Suckow's literary legacy but also ensures her stories resonate with contemporary audiences, bridging Iowa's rich literary history with today's readers.

item.title: Elon Musk's Cybercab rollout puts US safety rules to test as NHTSA audits 1,000 cars
item.description: Tesla's new Cybercab robotaxis are now operating in Texas without traditional controls. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an audit of these vehicles. US safety regulations were primarily designed for human-driven cars. Tesla's strategy relies on self-driving software and robotics for its valuation. Experts suggest Tesla may challenge regulatory interpretations to deploy its vehicles.

item.title: Israel released 28 wild donkeys in desert; 44 years later, they created an oasis
item.description: In an effort to rejuvenate the parched landscape of Israel's Ramon Crater, wild donkeys were brought back into the ecosystem. These resilient animals played a crucial role by creating waterholes, which became essential for desert wildlife. Additionally, their droppings helped spread acacia seeds, promoting the growth of trees. Their natural movements resulted in water-retaining depressions, significantly transforming the area's ecology into a thriving environment that has caught global attention.

item.title: Anthropic CEO calls for slowing down AI race; Altman & Musk back him up
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls for slowing AI development pace. He warns unchecked progress risks human understanding and control of powerful systems. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla chief Elon Musk support this urgent call. Recent AI testing revealed concerning behaviors and potential cybersecurity threats. Amodei believes careful development ensures AI's significant benefits for humanity.

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35m mansion: Why are neighbours worried about lake views?
item.description: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million waterfront mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio, has faced an unexpected neighborhood dispute over proposed fencing. Some residents reportedly worried the original plans could interfere with their Lake Erie views, leading to discussions with neighbors. A section of the fence extending toward the beach was later scrapped. Despite the disagreement, local officials have welcomed Kelce, while emphasizing the importance of both community ties and privacy.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s $6.7m estate: Why did his Cheshire mansion lose value?
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo’s former Cheshire estate was listed for about $7.4 million in 2023 but later saw its asking price fall to $6.7 million. The 23-acre property has a seven-bedroom mansion, indoor pool, gym, cinema, tennis and padel courts. Ronaldo moved there after returning to Manchester United but later relocated before leaving England for Al-Nassr.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: 'I definitely know how his mind works': Shreyas Iyer on Gautam Gambhir
item.description: Shreyas Iyer and Gautam Gambhir have worked together at Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), where they helped the franchise win the IPL title in 2024. Iyer was the captain, while Gambhir was the mentor. Iyer believes Gambhir's aggressive approach and his ability to understand individual players can help the team stay clear about their roles.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Decomposed body of ‘Pak Jaish terrorist’, M4 rifle found in J&K's Doda
item.description: Authorities in Doda's Divshetar have discovered the decomposed body of a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist from Pakistan. The remains, thought to have been buried in snow for some time after a previous operation, were found with an M4 rifle. Security forces are currently working to determine the identity of the individual as part of a broader investigation following recent encounters in the Jammu region.
item.dc:creator: SANJAY KHAJURIA

item.title: SIA searches Poonch, Udhampur in J&K 'radicalisation' probe
item.description: Jammu and Kashmir State Investigation Agency searched five locations Saturday. These searches occurred in Poonch and Udhampur districts for investigations. The agency is probing alleged secessionist narratives spread through online and offline channels. Investigators found individuals contacted suspicious persons across the Line of Control. Officials will share more details after the searches conclude.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: 'Zero tolerance' on terror: Brics declaration strongly condemns Pahalgam attack
item.description: Brics countries strongly condemned the Pahalgam terrorist attack, reaffirming their commitment to combating terrorism. The New Delhi Declaration 2026 opposed double standards and called for zero tolerance towards terrorism. It also supported comprehensive UN reform, including Security Council expansion for developing nations. China and Russia reiterated support for India and Brazil's greater UN roles. The declaration also raised concerns over trade measures and unilateral sanctions.

item.title: 'Pyramid of privilege': PM Modi takes shot at West, bats for Global South
item.description: During the BRICS summit, Prime Minister Modi emphasized the necessity for a global governance reset. He presented a comprehensive roadmap for future BRICS reforms, highlighting the need for increased decision-making power for the Global South. Modi also called for urgent changes to institutions like the UN Security Council and proposed establishing a BRICS continuity mechanism to ensure ongoing dialogues.

item.title: From Iraq to Yemen: How Iran-linked groups are putting Saudi energy routes under pressure
item.description: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its East-West oil pipeline after a drone attack. This vital energy conduit transports millions of barrels of crude oil daily. The attack has increased pressure on Iraq and raised global supply concerns. Houthi rebels in Yemen have also advanced along the Red Sea route. These events disrupt major energy and shipping routes worldwide.

item.title: Brics nations to have a common currency? Here’s what MEA said
item.description: Brics nations are discussing local currency trade settlements to reduce transaction costs. There is currently no proposal for a common Brics currency among member states. This initiative aims to complement existing global payment systems and improve trade efficiency. Leaders also addressed trade barriers and the need for a strong WTO. Discussions followed eight months of work under India's Brics chairship.

item.title: Which countries are home to the largest number of Indian migrants?
item.description: United Arab Emirates and the United States host the largest Indian-born populations abroad. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan follow with significant numbers of Indian emigrants. Kuwait, the United Kingdom, and Canada also have substantial Indian communities. Australia, Oman, and Qatar are other key destinations for Indian migrants. These figures highlight the Gulf's significant role in Indian overseas migration.

item.title: Russia’s new drone strategy: How jet-powered Gerans are changing the economics of warfare
item.description: Throughout August, Russia ramped up its use of jet-powered Geran drones, presenting a formidable challenge to Ukraine's air defenses due to their increased speed. In response, Ukraine is actively pursuing new interceptor missiles to combat this shifting threat. Simultaneously, Russia has been executing complex weekly attacks that combine a variety of weaponry aimed at overwhelming and complicating Ukrainian defense strategies.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: 'Even my shoelaces changed': Liam Neeson on becoming a father
item.description: Liam Neeson shares that becoming a father marked a significant turning point in his life. Research in neuroscience suggests that entering fatherhood alters brain function and hormone levels, deeply impacting a man's behavior. The ongoing journey of caregiving incites a series of biological shifts that make small adjustments become instinctual. Ultimately, these transformations reshape how one perceives everyday activities.

item.title: Happy Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: 50 wishes, messages and quotes for loved ones
item.description: Ganesh Chaturthi is a vibrant festival honoring Lord Ganesha, the deity of prosperity and fresh starts. Families invite Bappa into their homes, asking for his blessings of happiness and abundance. This article features a collection of heartfelt wishes and messages for sharing with friends and family, expressing hopes for wisdom, fortitude, and the eradication of challenges. The celebration is highlighted by prayers, joyful music, and cherished gatherings.

item.title: Joe Root creates history, breaks Sachin Tendulkar's Test record
item.description: Joe Root remained unbeaten on 62 off 69 balls, hitting nine fours, as England chased down 130 to complete a 3-0 Test series whitewash. His unbeaten half-century took his tally of Test fifties to 69, moving him past Tendulkar’s 68. West Indies great Shivnarine Chanderpaul is third on the list with 66 fifties, while Allan Border and Rahul Dravid have 63 each. Ricky Ponting has 62.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Floor Area Ratio explained: Why does it matter as Delhi grapples with building collapses
item.description: The recent building collapse in Delhi serves as a pivotal moment for the city's Master Plan aimed at redevelopment. This new approach proposes an increase in the Floor Area Ratio for older buildings, to replace dilapidated structures. By allowing greater construction on existing lots, this strategy seeks to address land shortages while enhancing urban infrastructure in Indian cities.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
